purpose: Independent practice of A6.11 — naming all six partners of 5 and connecting each addition fact to its related subtraction.
student_learning_goal: I can say all the ways to make 5 with two groups, and I can say what is left when I take some away.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can say all the ways to make 5 with two groups, and I can say what is left when I take some away.
header.character_watermark: Penny the Lead Coin Counter in the top-right corner of the header, holding a snap-cube tower of 5. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Look at each ten-frame. Some cells have red cubes and some have yellow cubes. Write the equation under each frame: __ + __ = 5.
parts.visual_layout: Top half of the page. Six ten-frames printed in a 2×3 grid, each ~2in × 1in. Each frame is pre-filled with a different partner of 5: (a) 0 red + 5 yellow, (b) 1 red + 4 yellow, (c) 2 red + 3 yellow, (d) 3 red + 2 yellow, (e) 4 red + 1 yellow, (f) 5 red + 0 yellow. Below each frame is a short equation line: __ + __ = 5. A small Penny puppet icon sits in the top-right corner.

image_placeholders.description: Six ten-frames in a 2×3 grid, B&W line-art with red/yellow cube fills represented as solid-fill or pattern-fill circles in each frame's cells. Each frame ~2in × 1in. Order: (0,5), (1,4), (2,3), (3,2), (4,1), (5,0) reading L-to-R, top-to-bottom. Below each, a faint 'partners' label space.
image_placeholders.placement: Top half of the page; 2×3 grid spanning full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P1_SIX_TEN_FRAMES at top half: keywords (ten-frame, partners, cubes) name what the image shows.

parts.answer_key: Six equations, in order: 0+5=5; 1+4=5; 2+3=5; 3+2=5; 4+1=5; 5+0=5. Accept any partner equation that matches the visible cube counts.

parts.student_instructions: Penny is hiding some cubes under her hand! Look at how many are showing. Write how many are hiding, then write the take-away equation: 5 − __ = __.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Three Partner Hunt scenes side-by-side. Each scene: a horizontal strip of 5 cubes with Penny's hand drawn covering some. Scene A shows 3 cubes visible (hand covers 2). Scene B shows 1 cube visible (hand covers 4). Scene C shows 4 cubes visible (hand covers 1). Below each scene, a blank line for hidden count and a take-away equation: 5 − __ = __.

image_placeholders.description: Three horizontal cube-tower scenes side-by-side, each ~2in × 1.5in, B&W line-art. Each scene shows a row of 5 snap-cubes. Penny's chef hand (~1in) covers some cubes; the visible cubes are clearly delineated. Scene A: 3 visible, hand covers 2. Scene B: 1 visible, hand covers 4. Scene C: 4 visible, hand covers 1. Penny's chef hat shows in the top of the hand illustration.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; three scenes spanning full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P2_PARTNER_HUNT_SCENES at middle: keywords (penny, cubes, hidden, showing) name what the image shows.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 2 hidden, 5 − 2 = 3. Scene B: 4 hidden, 5 − 4 = 1. Scene C: 1 hidden, 5 − 1 = 4.

parts.student_instructions: Colour in two ten-frames to show your own partners of 5. Then write your partner equation. Look — is your partner the SAME or DIFFERENT from your friend's?
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. Two empty ten-frames printed side by side, each ~2.5in × 1.2in. All cells unfilled (light-grey outlines for colouring). Below each frame, a writing line: __ + __ = 5. To the right of the frames, two small circles labelled SAME and DIFFERENT — the child circles one to compare to a partner sibling worksheet.

image_placeholders.description: Two empty ten-frames in B&W line-art, each ~2.5in × 1.2in, side by side. All 10 cells per frame unfilled with light-grey outlines suitable for crayon colouring. Below each, an equation line. To the right, the SAME / DIFFERENT comparison circles.
image_placeholders.placement: Bottom half of the page; two frames spanning the page width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P3_TWO_EMPTY_TEN_FRAMES at bottom: keywords (ten-frame, partner, same, different) name what the image shows.

parts.answer_key: Any valid partner of 5 in each frame. A response is correct if (a) the cube counts match the equation written, (b) the equation totals 5. Accept any partner: 0+5, 1+4, 2+3, 3+2, 4+1, 5+0. The SAME/DIFFERENT circle is reflective; either choice is acceptable as long as the child can articulate why.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and find partners for a NEW number — try partners of 4, or partners of 6!
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation. Hand out at the end of the Partner Hunt game. Most children should complete Parts 1 and 2 independently if they were successful at the partner game. Part 3 is the diagnostic stretch — children who write a non-partner-of-5 (e.g. 4+2=6) need a re-loop on the partner concept before Lesson 3. Mark Part 1 instant-recall children for the formative tracker.
